newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWIMMING-WORLD RECORD FOR POLL, MIXED DAY FOR VOELKER.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-WORLD RECORD FOR POLL, MIXED DAY FOR VOELKER.

text.p: Olympic champion Claudia Poll obliterated her own world record while disqualification denied Sandra Voelker a rare double on a dramatic night at the world short-course swimming championships on Friday.

Fifteen-year-old Australians Kristy Ellem and Natasha Bowron romped away with gold medals and four of their male team mates eclipsed a relay record to keep Australia top of the medal heap with six titles.
Poll produced the outstanding swim and first individual world record on the second day of the four-day championships with a majestic victory in the women's 200 metres freestyle.

The 24-year-old Costa Rican seized the lead from Germany's early pace-setter Antje Buschschulte and swept home in one minute 54.17 seconds to win by over two seconds from China's Nian Yin and Slovakia's Martina Moravcova.
The time shattered the old mark of 1:55.42 with which she won the title at the last world short-course championships in Rio de Janeiro in December 1995.
"I knew about two weeks ago that I could do it," said Poll, who upstaged German favourite Franziska van Almsick to secure her 1996 Olympic triumph in Atlanta.
"My coach knew it in February but I didn't believe him right away. When I heard the crowd cheering in the last 50 metres I just thought it's even better than the last one."

Voelker experienced a day of conflicting emotions, starting with a European record (24.62) in the morning's 50 metres freestyle heats and ending in the frustration of disqualification after she had touched first in the 100 backstroke final.

In between, she won the 50 freestyle final by 0.08 seconds from American Jenny Thompson, who had beaten her to the gold in Thursday's 100 freestyle. Defending champion Le Jingyi of China was a further 0.05 behind in third place.
Later came the blemish of disqualification after she had touched first in 59.50, 0.25 seconds ahead of China's Lu Donghua, in the 100 backstroke final.
The 23-year-old German was ruled out for swimming under water more than the 15 metres allowed after the start.
"Yes, I knew because I was over the line. They say 15 metres but I think it's a bit unfair because at the World Cup lots of people went further," Voelker said.
Australia, who had broken the men's 4x100 medley relay world mark on Thursday, claimed another short-course world record in the 4x200 freestyle relay.
Michael Klim, Grant Hackett, Bill Kirby and Matthew Dunn powered to victory in 7:02.74 to beat the 7:05.17 mark set by a West German quartet in February 1986.

Fellow Australian, Ellem inherited the title of training partner Samantha Riley, winning the 200 breaststroke by nearly three seconds from Romania's Larisa Lacusta in 2:22.68 to make her the third-fastest swimmer in the event ever.
Bowron led the 800 freestyle from start to finish, winning by nearly two seconds in 8:26.45 from fast-finishing German Kerstin Kielgass, 12 years her senior at 27.
Cuba retained the men's 200 backstroke title, Neisser Bent snatching a last-gasp victory to inherit the crown relinquished by compatriot Rodolfo Falcon, who failed to make the final.

Swedish fans roared their approval as Patrik Isaksson sprinted to a gritty victory in the 100 breaststroke and they were also generous in their celebration of a surprise win for neighbours Denmark when Jacob Carstensen snatched gold in a desperately close 400 freestyle.
A mere 0.49 seconds separated the first five at the end of the 16-length race, with the 18-year-old Dane just edging out American Chad Carvin for the gold.
